novel.justification: For an ordered three-dose benefit-risk outcome, this condition permits monotone improvement, monotone deterioration, an interior optimum, and all ties; it excludes only an individual whose middle dose is strictly worse than both extremes. Such a restriction is substantively interpretable when efficacy rises and toxicity also rises with dose.

assumptions.condition: \(O_1,\ldots,O_N\) are independent and identically distributed under \(P\).

definitions.name: Prespecified ordinal benefit-risk scoring rule
definitions.construction: Fix clinically interpretable efficacy score \(E(d)\), toxicity burden \(H(d)\), positive weights \(w_E,w_H\), and cutpoints \(c_j\) before unblinding. Set \(U_{\mathrm{BR}}(d)=w_EE(d)-w_HH(d)\) and \(Y(d)=\sum_{j=1}^{L-1}\mathbf 1\{U_{\mathrm{BR}}(d)\ge c_j\}\in\mathcal Y_L\).

definitions.name: Marginally compatible non-valley couplings
definitions.construction: \(\Gamma_L(p)=\{q\in\Delta(\mathcal U_L):\sum_{u\in\mathcal U_L:u_d=j}q(u)=p_{dj}\ \text{for every }d\in\mathcal D,\ j\in\mathcal Y_L\}\).

definitions.name: Primitive canonical full-facet rows
definitions.construction: \(\mathcal H_L=\{h\in\mathbb Z^{3L+1}:s_h(u)\ge0\ \forall u\in\mathcal U_L,\ \gcd(h)=1,\ \operatorname{aff}\{v_L(u):s_h(u)=0\}\ \text{has dimension }3L-1\}\), where the valid orientation is chosen and \(\alpha_{d0}=0\).

definitions.name: Two-pass bounded triangular-affine source checker
definitions.construction: \(\mathsf{CHECK}_{2\mathrm{BTAS}}(S)=1\) exactly when \(S\) is a finite-state program, independent of \(L\), with at most sixteen signed-integer registers; it makes two left-to-right scans of the \(L-1\) nonbaseline levels; every register initializer is affine in \(L\); in one cell, register \(r_k\) is updated to an affine combination of the cell label, \(L\), constants of absolute value at most seven, and pre-update registers \(r_1,\ldots,r_k\); acceptance and branching depend only on the finite label state and boundary position; row emission is affine in the final registers; and no branch queries a register value, slack, rank, validity, facetness, or an external table.

definitions.name: Three-letter staircase facet family
definitions.construction: For \(n=L-1\ge2\) and \(\omega\in\{\mathrm L,\mathrm R,\mathrm D\}^{n-1}\) ending in \(\mathrm D\), initialize \(a_0=c_0=0\); set \(d_j=a_{j-1}+c_{j-1}+1\), update \(a_j=d_j\) for letters \(\mathrm L\) or \(\mathrm D\) and otherwise \(a_j=a_{j-1}\), and update \(c_j=d_j\) for letters \(\mathrm R\) or \(\mathrm D\) and otherwise \(c_j=c_{j-1}\). With \(K=a_{n-1}=c_{n-1}\), emit \(\kappa=K\), \(\beta=(0,-K-1,0)\), \(\alpha_{0j}=-a_j\), \(\alpha_{1j}=d_j\), \(\alpha_{2j}=-c_j\) for \(j<n\), and \(\alpha_{0n},\alpha_{1n},\alpha_{2n}=(-K,2K+1,-K)\).

definitions.name: Prefix-extremizer rank-state synthesis handle
definitions.construction: Partition a valid row by which prefix and suffix argmin sets attain each of the five legal Cartesian-product slack minima at every middle level; augment this label by the rank increments of the tight response-type rows; quotient labels that induce the same renormalized deletion and successor actions; then synthesize the finite transition labels and triangular register coordinates from these geometric actions, with the staircase family in \(\text{def:staircase-family}\) as a mandatory stress-test sublanguage.

definitions.name: Three-facet endpoint certificates
definitions.construction: Write each \(h_i\in\mathcal H_L\) as \(a_i(p)+\beta_i^\top\theta\ge0\). For \(d\in\mathcal D\), \(\mathcal D_d^-\) contains every nonnegative vector \(\lambda\) supported on at most three linearly independent \(\beta_i\) with \(\sum_i\lambda_i\beta_i=e_d\), and \(\mathcal D_d^+\) contains every nonnegative vector \(\mu\) supported on at most three linearly independent \(\beta_i\) with \(\sum_i\mu_i\beta_i=-e_d\).

definitions.name: Exact pilot-localized multinomial inversion handle
definitions.construction: Split \(N\) observations deterministically into a pilot of size \(\lfloor N^{2/3}\rfloor\) and a main sample. Form an exact pilot product-simplex region with error budget \(\delta_N=\min\{\alpha/2,N^{-2}\}\). If one endpoint contrast is optimal throughout that region, invert its exact conditional product-multinomial distribution on the main sample; otherwise invert every retained contrast from \(\mathcal D_d^-\) and \(\mathcal D_d^+\) with a common Bonferroni allocation and map the intervals through the finite max-min formulas. Empty arms return the logical endpoint range.

statements.statement: For every \(P\in\mathcal P_L\), the observed law identifies \(p_{dj}=P(Y=j\mid A=d)\), and the identified set for \(\theta(q)\) is exactly \(\{\theta(q):q\in\Gamma_L(p)\}\).
statements.justification: This establishes that the geometric object is the sharp causal identified set rather than a relaxation.
statements.gap: Generic response-type reductions are known, but the equality is stated here for the exact non-valley and unique-peak objects used throughout.
statements.consumer: A randomized three-dose trial can use the bounds for a prespecified ordinal benefit-risk score in a conditional sensitivity analysis without introducing cross-world independence.

statements.statement: For every \(L\ge2\), \(\dim(Q_{3,L})=3L\). For every \(L\ge3\), the construction in \(\text{def:staircase-family}\) maps the \(3^{L-3}\) words ending in \(\mathrm D\) injectively into \(\mathcal W_L\); the all-\(\mathrm D\) word has coefficients \(2^j-1\), and alternating \(\mathrm L\) and \(\mathrm R\) prefixes attain \(\operatorname{Fib}(L)-1\) at the last common endpoint coefficient.
statements.justification: The family supplies an exponential lower bound, explicit weighted facets, and the mandatory encoding stress test.
statements.gap: Bonet2001 establishes a causal facet precedent, but no published result exhibits this non-valley staircase family or its Fibonacci and doubling subfamilies.
statements.consumer: Any claimed complete generator or coefficient-size bound can be falsified immediately on this explicit family.

statements.statement: Does the prefix-extremizer rank-state handle yield a finite set \(\mathsf T\), a renormalized geometric predecessor for every row in \(\mathcal H_{L+1}\), and one fixed program \(S_\star\) with \(\mathsf{CHECK}_{2\mathrm{BTAS}}(S_\star)=1\) such that, for every \(L\ge2\), the output multiset satisfies \(\operatorname{Out}_L(S_\star)=\mathcal H_L\) with multiplicity one, every emitted row is sound, and every canonical cut or weighted facet is emitted? The derived predecessor must give inverse type-labelled successors and include every staircase word from \(\text{def:staircase-family}\).
statements.justification: This is the theorem-level kernel: it upgrades finite hull computation to a uniform analytic and uniquely enumerable facet system.
statements.gap: Russell2021 supplies a general sharp-bound program for continuous functionals of the joint law of two potential outcomes, DuarteEtAl2024 gives generic sharp numerical optimization, AvisFukuda1996 gives abstract reverse search, and KaidoPonomarev2025 gives graph-based support inequalities. None proves a dimension-uniform facet grammar after a genuinely three-marginal forbidden-support deletion under the stated syntactic restriction.
statements.consumer: The complete stream makes every sharp unique-best endpoint auditable and reproducible for arbitrary prespecified ordinal resolution.

statements.statement: If \(\text{oeq:complete-two-pass-facet-stream}\) has a positive solution, its geometric successor table determines a fixed matrix \(T_\star\) and finite initial vector \(c_2\) such that \(c_{L+1}=T_\star c_L\) and \(F_L=\mathbf 1^\top c_L\) for every \(L\ge2\); the initial values satisfy \(F_2=7\), \(F_3=59\), \(F_4=197\), and \(F_5=721\).
statements.justification: A geometric transfer law is the falsifiable enumeration consequence of the finite predecessor theorem.
statements.gap: Finite hull counts can always be fit by an ad hoc recurrence; the claim requires the recurrence to be derived from the same sound and unique successor types.
statements.consumer: Researchers can know catalogue size and generation cost before computing bounds at a chosen ordinal resolution.

statements.statement: For every compatible \(p\) and \(d\in\mathcal D\), \(\underline\theta_d(p)=\max_{\lambda\in\mathcal D_d^-}-\sum_i\lambda_i a_i(p)\) and \(\overline\theta_d(p)=\min_{\mu\in\mathcal D_d^+}\sum_i\mu_i a_i(p)\). Every certificate uses at most three full facets, and three cannot be replaced uniformly by two: at \(L=2\) and \(p_{0,1}=p_{1,1}=p_{2,1}=1/2\), the sharp upper endpoint \(\overline\theta_1(p)=1/4\) requires three canonical full-facet normals.
statements.justification: This converts the full mixed-target facet system into evaluable sharp scalar endpoints and pins down the exact dual sparsity.
statements.gap: GabrielSachsJensen2024 derives sharp symbolic formulas for ordinal measures of benefit from two potential outcomes under binary treatment, Chiba2017 studies \(P\{Y(1)\ge Y(0)\}\) for binary treatment, and LuDingDasgupta2018 obtains cumulative formulas for two-arm ordinal benefit. The target here is the unique-best indicator among three potential outcomes after deleting strict-middle-valley triples; every two-coordinate projection remains unrestricted, and the sharp endpoint can require three canonical full-facet normals. Thus the three-facet conclusion concerns genuinely three-marginal forbidden-support geometry rather than a reformulation of a two-arm symbolic benefit formula.
statements.consumer: The six formulas support an abstract conditional sensitivity analysis of which psilocybin dose is uniquely best under the prespecified score and maintained cross-world restriction.

statements.statement: For every compatible \(p\), dose \(d\), and endpoint in \(\{\underline\theta_d(p),\overline\theta_d(p)\}\), there exists \(q^\star\in\Gamma_L(p)\) attaining that endpoint with \(|\operatorname{supp}(q^\star)|\le3L-2\). For rational \(p\), one can construct \(q^\star\) with rational masses from the active facet certificate and complementary slackness.
statements.justification: Sharpness requires compatible response-triple laws, not only valid dual inequalities.
statements.gap: Two-way constructive tables are available in LuDingDasgupta2018; the present construction must honor a forbidden three-way support at every endpoint branch.
statements.consumer: Endpoint-attaining mixtures provide transparent worst-case response profiles for benefit-risk reporting and sensitivity analysis.

statements.statement: Can the exact pilot-localized multinomial inversion handle be completed so that \(\inf_{P\in\mathcal P_L}P\{(\underline\theta_d(p),\overline\theta_d(p))_{d\in\mathcal D}\in\mathcal I_{N,1-\alpha}\}\ge1-\alpha\) for every \(N\), including empty arms, zero cells, and tied active facets, while at each fixed positive-support law with one separated active contrast and positive contrast variance the corresponding scalar side of \(\mathcal I_{N,1-\alpha}\) is asymptotically equivalent to the semiparametrically efficient Wald interval?
statements.justification: Identification without boundary-valid uncertainty quantification is inadequate for sparse multi-arm ordinal trials.
statements.gap: ChoRussell2024 perturbs LPs for uniform validity and FangSantos2019 simulates directional derivatives; neither delivers finite-sample support honesty plus pointwise efficient scalar adaptation for this six-endpoint map.
statements.consumer: The result supplies a single prespecified report that remains honest in small trial cells without paying a permanent efficiency penalty on regular faces.

statements.statement: When \(L=2\), \(Q_{3,2}\) is a full-dimensional unimodular simplex with seven primitive facets. At \(p_{0,1}=p_{1,1}=p_{2,1}=1/2\), the middle-dose endpoint interval is \([\underline\theta_1(p),\overline\theta_1(p)]=[0,1/4]\), attained respectively by mixtures on \(\{000,111\}\) and \(\{001,010,100,111\}\).
statements.justification: The binary reduction checks normalization, dimension, sharpness, and attainment against an exactly invertible base case.
statements.gap: This is a required reduction rather than a novelty claim.
statements.consumer: It anchors the transfer recurrence and supplies a hand-checkable validation case for software and empirical workflows.

sampling_model.design: Three-arm randomized experiment with known assignment probabilities \(\pi_d\).
sampling_model.units: Independent units with the potential efficacy and toxicity components mapped by \(\text{def:prespecified-benefit-risk-score}\) to an ordinal response triple supported on \(\mathcal U_L\).
sampling_model.treatment: Observed dose \(A\in\{0,1,2\}\) and observed prespecified ordinal benefit-risk score \(Y=Y(A)\).
sampling_model.overlap: \(\min_{d\in\mathcal D}\pi_d>0\), with realized empty arms handled by the exact fallback.
sampling_model.nuisance_estimation: Arm-specific multinomial probabilities \(p_{dj}\) are estimated by randomized-arm empirical frequencies; exact inference conditions on realized arm counts.

comparator_promise_table.comparator_claim: Discrete causal bounds can be computed as polynomial programs with convergent anytime outer bounds.
Finite causal response-type models can have complete observable facet inequalities beyond Pearl's basic instrumental inequality.
A deterministic parent map supports duplicate-free reverse-search enumeration without storing visited objects.
Two-arm ordinal probabilities of benefit and strict benefit have sharp cumulative closed-form bounds with constructive attainment.
Two-potential-outcome distributional bounds under support restrictions admit a Kantorovich-dual characterization.
Multi-potential-outcome partial identification is representable as multi-marginal optimal transport, with plug-in rates for quadratic objectives.
General potential-response support restrictions have sharp graph-based observable implications, with extra inequalities in nonregular cases.
Randomly perturbed LP value functions yield uniformly valid confidence sets for linear functionals of set-identified parameters.
For Gaussian first-stage limits, ordinary bootstrap consistency is equivalent to full differentiability, and a derivative-estimation bootstrap handles directional maps.
Intersection bounds admit adaptive inequality selection and Gaussian-process inference.

Continuous functionals of the joint distribution of the two potential outcomes in a binary-treatment model admit sharp bounds obtained through random-set core-determining restrictions and convex optimization.

For a binary treatment and ordinal outcome, the two-potential-outcome probability \(P\{Y(1)\ge Y(0)\}\) has sharp nonparametric sample bounds, and exact randomization procedures are available under the paper's stated conditions.
Two-arm ordinal measures of benefit, no harm, and relative treatment effect admit sharp symbolic nonparametric bounds in the designs analyzed in the paper.

tldr: Randomization identifies the three marginals of a prespecified ordinal benefit-risk score but not the population shares for which each dose is uniquely best. Under weak individual unimodality, the compatible target vectors form a structured three-marginal polytope. The central open question is whether every primitive facet of this polytope admits a finite geometric predecessor type and is generated exactly once by one fixed, oracle-free, sixteen-register two-pass triangular-affine stream. A positive answer gives an analytic all-support facet catalogue and a fixed transfer recurrence; the resulting catalogue yields sharp endpoint formulas using at most three full facets, endpoint-attaining latent mixtures, and a route to exact support-aware simultaneous inference that becomes scalar efficient on separated positive-support faces. The psilocybin example is only an abstract conditional sensitivity analysis: randomization identifies score marginals, whereas the trial neither identifies nor clinically validates weak individual unimodality.

project_justification.gap: Russell (2021) sharply bounds continuous functionals of the joint law of two potential outcomes in a binary-treatment model, Chiba (2017) bounds and develops randomization inference for \(P\{Y(1)\ge Y(0)\}\) with two ordinal potential outcomes, and Gabriel, Sachs, and Jensen (2024) derive sharp symbolic ordinal-benefit formulas in two-arm designs. Generic discrete causal optimizers and multi-marginal transport solvers return numerical values. None classifies the primitive supporting inequalities of the three-dose non-valley coupling polytope for every finite ordinal support, proves a finite predecessor calculus, or compiles such a calculus into an exact-once bounded-register stream; the three-facet endpoint result addresses a unique-best indicator whose forbidden-support geometry is invisible in every two-arm projection.
project_justification.niche: The non-valley support is genuinely three-way: every two-coordinate projection of \(\mathcal U_L\) is the unrestricted square \(\mathcal Y_L^2\), even though the full support deletes triples with \(u_0>u_1\) and \(u_2>u_1\). The first new step is therefore minimization of candidate affine slack over that non-Cartesian three-marginal support, followed by tight-row rank classification. Pairwise Hall inequalities and regular compatibility-graph arguments miss weighted full facets, while generic hull enumeration does not explain the observed staircase, doubling, and Fibonacci coefficient families.
project_justification.fill: The project isolates tight-product extremizer and rank signatures, seeks a finite renormalized predecessor classification, and requires a literal \(\texttt{CHECK\_2BTAS}\)-accepted source whose soundness, completeness, and uniqueness are mathematical claims. The same representation is then projected to sharp unique-best endpoints and coupled to exact multinomial inference with an explicit regular-face efficiency target.

related_work: Russell (2021) studies continuous functionals of the joint distribution of the two potential outcomes \(Y(0)\) and \(Y(1)\) in a binary-treatment model, using random-set core-determining restrictions and convex optimization to obtain sharp bounds; that general two-potential-outcome method informs the optimization layer but does not classify a three-marginal forbidden-support polytope. Chiba (2017) studies the binary-treatment ordinal parameter \(P\{Y(1)\ge Y(0)\}\), gives numerical sharp nonparametric sample bounds, and develops exact randomization inference under the paper's stated conditions; its response type is likewise a pair \(Y(0),Y(1)\). Lu, Ding, and Dasgupta (2018) derive cumulative sharp bounds and attaining tables for two-arm ordinal benefit probabilities; their construction motivates the endpoint layer but does not cover a three-way forbidden support. Gabriel, Sachs, and Jensen (2024) derive sharp symbolic formulas for ordinal measures of benefit, no harm, and relative treatment effect in two-arm designs; those formulas concern two potential outcomes, whereas \(\text{thm:sharp-three-facet-endpoints}\) targets the unique-best indicator among three potential outcomes under a forbidden-three-way-support restriction and can require three full-facet normals. The first genuinely three-marginal step not subsumed by Russell (2021), Chiba (2017), Gabriel, Sachs, and Jensen (2024), or the other two-arm results is that every two-coordinate projection of \(\mathcal U_L\) equals \(\mathcal Y_L^2\), yet the full coupling must delete exactly the triples with \(u_0>u_1\) and \(u_2>u_1\); validity therefore starts by minimizing each candidate affine slack over this non-Cartesian three-way support before tight-row ranks and facets can be classified. Duarte et al. (2024) prove a general polynomial-program representation and an anytime route to sharp discrete causal bounds; this project is informed by that framework but targets an analytic, canonical, dimension-uniform facet system. Bonet (2001) shows that causal response-type models can demand complete observable facet inequalities, providing the closest causal-polytope precedent. Avis and Fukuda (1996) show how a canonical parent forest yields duplicate-free enumeration without a visited set, which motivates the unique-predecessor requirement. Kim (2014) embeds support restrictions in a two-marginal Kantorovich dual. Gao, Ge, and Qian (2025) establish general multi-marginal optimal-transport identification and rates for quadratic objectives, but their variational machinery does not yield these indicator-cost facets. Kaido and Ponomarev (2025) characterize sharp support-restriction implications using compatibility graphs; the present non-valley support violates their regular maximal-clique correspondence and adds unique-peak coordinates. Cho and Russell (2024), Fang and Santos (2019), and Chernozhukov, Lee, and Rosen (2013) inform the inference handle through perturbed LP values, directional derivatives, and binding-set localization. Goodwin et al. (2022) supply a randomized three-dose setting with efficacy and adverse-event measurements from which the fixed score in \(\text{def:prespecified-benefit-risk-score}\) could be prespecified. The proposed use is only an abstract conditional sensitivity analysis under weak individual unimodality: the trial identifies the randomized-arm score marginals but neither identifies the cross-world restriction nor clinically validates it.
technical_internal_limitation: The presolve proves explicit staircase facets and gives exact rational small-support certificates, but it does not construct the complete predecessor type set or an accepted source. In particular, the direct two-register implementation of alternating \(\mathrm L\) and \(\mathrm R\) staircase updates violates either fixed triangular order. The main open question must therefore produce a different representation within sixteen registers or prove that the source contract is impossible. The inference handle also leaves exact semialgebraic computation and the regular-face quantile transfer to be established.
honest_scope: The all-\(L\) full-facet stream, finite type theorem, transfer matrix, and adaptive exact inference are open. The finite counts \(59\), \(197\), and \(721\), the staircase family, and the three-facet projection are presolve evidence to be independently proved within the project. Under \(L=2\), the proposal must reduce to the seven-facet simplex and the middle-dose interval \([0,1/4]\) at equal Bernoulli marginals. The Goodwin et al. use case is an abstract conditional sensitivity analysis based on the prespecified score in \(\text{def:prespecified-benefit-risk-score}\). Random assignment and consistency identify its arm marginals, but the trial neither identifies nor clinically validates weak individual unimodality; no empirical verification of that cross-world restriction, clinical validation, or data analysis is claimed.

seed_details.opportunity: Classify every primitive facet of the three-dose non-valley coupling polytope and compile the classification into one fixed exact-once bounded-register stream.
seed_details.first_changed_proof_step: Replace the generic polynomial-program reduction and branch-and-bound search by a classification of the five prefix/suffix tight-product types and their augmented-rank transitions.
seed_details.destination_search: Searches for three-treatment ordinal unique-best facets, non-valley coupling polytopes, and all-support facet recurrences found Russell2021 general two-potential-outcome sharp-bound optimization, numerical discrete optimizers, and generic multi-marginal transport, but no matching analytic catalogue.
seed_details.cynical_objection: Immediate from DuarteEtAl2024 because the target is a finite discrete causal bound.
seed_details.rebuttal: DuarteEtAl2024 proves reduction to polynomial optimization and asymptotic sharpness of an anytime solver; it does not give an irredundant symbolic H-representation, a unique predecessor map, or a fixed all-support counting recurrence.

seed_details.opportunity: Derive finite max-min formulas for all six unique-best endpoints and prove that three full facets always suffice and are sometimes necessary.
seed_details.first_changed_proof_step: Replace the lower- or upper-triangular two-way coupling constructed from cumulative inequalities by an extreme dual decomposition in the three target coordinates followed by a forbidden-support completion.
seed_details.destination_search: Searches for three-arm ordinal unique-best probabilities and symbolic multi-marginal benefit bounds found Chiba2017, GabrielSachsJensen2024, and related two-potential-outcome ordinal formulas, plus generic transport programs, but no three-way forbidden-support endpoint system.
seed_details.cynical_objection: Immediate from finite linear-program duality because there are only three target coordinates.
seed_details.rebuttal: The support-three conclusion is generic polyhedral input, but the publishable content requires the complete canonical facet family, explicit endpoint branches, necessity of three, and response-triple mixtures at ties and zero cells.

seed_details.opportunity: Permit an \(\varepsilon\)-share of strict middle valleys and derive the piecewise-affine critical violation mass at which each positive unique-best lower bound disappears.
seed_details.first_changed_proof_step: Replace the conditional \(c\)-dependence and rank-invariance relaxation by a mass budget on a named forbidden response-type subset inside a three-marginal transport dual.
seed_details.destination_search: Searches pairing ordinal unimodality violations with breakdown frontiers found IV monotonicity relaxations and generic assumption deletion, but no strict-middle-valley mass frontier.
seed_details.cynical_objection: Immediate from MastenPoirier2020 after renaming the relaxation parameter.
seed_details.rebuttal: The relaxed feasible set here changes a three-way forbidden support, so its breakpoints and active weighted facets are not the binary-selection frontier of Masten and Poirier.

seed_details.opportunity: Construct one simultaneous confidence region for all six endpoint coordinates that remains honest at support loss and facet ties while reducing to efficient scalar Wald inference on separated faces.
seed_details.first_changed_proof_step: Replace global random perturbation of an arbitrary linear program by exact conditional multinomial inversion on a pilot-localized active-facet set, with a full-support fallback.
seed_details.destination_search: Searches for support-adaptive simultaneous inference for finite max-min endpoint maps found perturbed-LP coverage and directional bootstrap theory, but no procedure combining zero-cell honesty with regular-face scalar efficiency.
seed_details.cynical_objection: Immediate from ChoRussell2024 or FangSantos2019 because endpoint maps are finite maxima and minima.
seed_details.rebuttal: Those papers diagnose or regularize non-smooth value maps, but do not provide exact support-aware six-coordinate coverage together with oracle scalar efficiency when arm cells and endpoint variances can vanish.

seed_details.anchor: Bonet2001, Sections 2--3 and the discrete instrumental-test construction
seed_details.opportunity: Characterize why the non-valley support evades pairwise compatibility graphs and derive a minimal higher-order hypergraph inequality basis for its observable-and-target projection.
seed_details.first_changed_proof_step: Replace pairwise compatibility edges by three-uniform legal-response hyperedges before taking the projected marginal-and-peak polytope.
seed_details.destination_search: The later KaidoPonomarev2025 graph framework covers general support restrictions, but its regular maximal-clique condition fails because all pairwise arm combinations are compatible while some triples are not.
seed_details.cynical_objection: Immediate from the general nonregular inequalities of KaidoPonomarev2025.
seed_details.rebuttal: Their graph expansion yields testable marginal inequalities; it does not classify the mixed peak-coordinate facets or give a bounded-state predecessor calculus for this hypergraph projection.

seed_details.opportunity: Build an output-sensitive reverse-search enumerator for canonical non-valley facets using a geometric parent map and no visited-output set.
seed_details.first_changed_proof_step: Replace generic spatial branch-and-bound nodes by facet-specific rank signatures and a canonical renormalized deletion parent.
seed_details.destination_search: AvisFukuda1996 supplies the exact-once parent-tree method, but searches found no specialization to response-type facet families with changing dimension.
seed_details.cynical_objection: Immediate from AvisFukuda1996 once adjacency is available.
seed_details.rebuttal: Adjacency and a terminating unique parent are precisely the missing geometric theorems; raw top-level deletion fails for most certified small-support facets.

seed_details.opportunity: Determine the exact exponential growth constant for the largest primitive facet coefficient and the minimal explicit representation length.
seed_details.first_changed_proof_step: Replace finite facet enumeration by all-support lower families and determinant-based upper bounds, then close the exponential-base gap.
seed_details.destination_search: Searches for coefficient growth of causal response-type polytopes found general determinant bounds but no result for the non-valley three-marginal family.
seed_details.cynical_objection: A Hadamard upper bound and one doubling family already settle the order, leaving only a combinatorial constant.
seed_details.rebuttal: The objection does not kill mathematical novelty but correctly limits consumer value; the seed is retained only as a supporting theorem, not the proposal kernel.

seed_details.anchor: LuDingDasgupta2018, Proposition 1 and constructive Supplementary Part A
seed_details.opportunity: Characterize the full six-dimensional set of lower and upper unique-best endpoints and determine which endpoint vectors are jointly attainable by one latent mixture.
seed_details.first_changed_proof_step: Replace separate triangular joint-table constructions by a common three-marginal coupling with simultaneous complementary-slackness conditions.
seed_details.destination_search: Searches found separately sharp pairwise ordinal benefit bounds but no joint attainability theorem for six three-dose endpoint coordinates.
seed_details.cynical_objection: The vector is merely the image of the same finite coupling polytope.
seed_details.rebuttal: Computability is immediate, but a closed joint-support-function system and constructive simultaneous attainment are not; the present project nevertheless prioritizes the more foundational complete facet stream.

seed_details.opportunity: Choose the dose maximizing the worst-case unique-best share under a strict-valley violation budget and derive a regret frontier against the oracle best dose.
seed_details.first_changed_proof_step: After deriving violation-indexed endpoint formulas, replace sign preservation by a finite robust treatment-choice comparison across three doses.
seed_details.destination_search: Searches for partial-identification policy choice with ordinal unique-best welfare found general maximin rules but no three-dose unimodality-regret frontier.
seed_details.cynical_objection: Once the endpoint frontier is known, choosing the largest lower bound is mechanical.
seed_details.rebuttal: A nontrivial policy theorem would require sampling regret and tie geometry beyond the identification frontier; that extra layer is not sufficiently developed for this version.

threads: DuarteEtAl2024, Theorem 1, turns a discrete causal query into a polynomial program and proves convergence to sharp bounds, but supplies neither symbolic facets nor an all-support recurrence.

Bonet2001 uses convex geometry to obtain complete observable instrumental inequalities in finite response-type models, establishing the facet-level precedent but not the present three-marginal peak projection.

AvisFukuda1996 derives duplicate-free enumeration from a deterministic local-search parent forest; the missing adaptation is a dimension-changing geometric parent computable by the restricted triangular stream.

KaidoPonomarev2025, Theorems 1--3 and Appendix D.3, gives sharp graph-based support inequalities. Its regular clique correspondence fails for the non-valley cube because pairwise compatibility does not detect a forbidden triple, and its nonregular algorithm does not classify mixed peak facets.

GaoGeQian2025 represents causal partial identification as multi-marginal optimal transport and proves rates for quadratic objectives, but does not provide a discrete analytic H-representation or an exact facet generator.

Russell2021, the article abstract and Supplementary Appendices 2--3, sharply bounds continuous functionals of the joint distribution of the two potential outcomes in a binary-treatment model through random-set restrictions and convex optimization; it does not analyze three potential-outcome marginals or an all-support facet grammar.
literature_map.settled: Finite response-type reduction, sharp optimization of continuous functionals of two-potential-outcome laws, generic discrete optimization, general reverse-search logic, and generic support-graph inequalities are settled.
literature_map.unoccupied_target: No located paper crosses the first genuinely three-marginal step: all pairwise projections of \(\mathcal U_L\) are unrestricted, but the full coupling deletes \(u_0>u_1\) and \(u_2>u_1\). No located result classifies the resulting tight affine-slack minima and ranks into finite all-\(L\) predecessor types or a fixed \(\texttt{CHECK\_2BTAS}\)-accepted exact-once source for the primitive facets of \(Q_{3,L}\).

threads: LuDingDasgupta2018, Proposition 1, gives cumulative closed forms and constructive joint tables for binary-treatment ordinal benefit.
Kim2014, Theorem 1, uses Kantorovich duality and dual level sets for two-potential-outcome support restrictions.
GaoGeQian2025 supplies the general multi-marginal transport identified set but leaves the present discrete indicator cost in variational form.
GabrielSachsJensen2024 derives symbolic two-arm benefit, no-harm, and relative-effect bounds in additional designs, without a three-arm unique-best object.

Chiba2017 studies the binary-treatment ordinal probability \(P\{Y(1)\ge Y(0)\}\), gives numerical sharp nonparametric sample bounds, and develops exact randomization inference under the paper's stated conditions; both the estimand and response-type table involve only the pair \(Y(0),Y(1)\).

Russell2021 covers continuous functionals of the joint distribution of two potential outcomes in a binary-treatment model, but its general convex program does not supply symbolic three-marginal unique-best endpoint formulas or the canonical facets used by those formulas.
literature_map.settled: Sharp optimization and randomization inference for selected two-potential-outcome functionals, two-arm cumulative formulas, constructive pairwise attainment, and generic multi-marginal optimization are settled.
literature_map.unoccupied_target: Because every pairwise projection of the non-valley support is unrestricted, neither two-potential-outcome scope detects the forbidden triple. No located result gives all six three-dose unique-best endpoints as finite combinations of canonical non-valley facets with a proof that three are sometimes necessary.

threads: MastenPoirier2020 defines breakdown frontiers and proves inference for a structured relaxation of identifying assumptions.
Noack2021 places a population-share budget on monotonicity-violating response types and obtains sharp IV sensitivity regions.
DuarteEtAl2024 allows assumptions to be relaxed inside a discrete polynomial program, providing a numerical verification route but no symbolic breakpoints.
LuDingDasgupta2018 provides the ordinal cumulative algebra to which the violation-mass budget must be coupled.
literature_map.settled: Critical-relaxation objects and violation-share sensitivity are established in other causal models.
literature_map.unoccupied_target: No located result derives the sharp piecewise-affine frontier for an \(\varepsilon\)-mass of strict middle valleys in a three-dose ordinal coupling.

threads: ChoRussell2024 obtains uniform inference by bootstrapping randomly perturbed LP value functions, with exact asymptotic coverage on an outer set rather than efficient inference on a selected regular face.
FangSantos2019 proves that the standard bootstrap is generally inconsistent for directionally but not fully differentiable maps and supplies a derivative-estimation bootstrap.
ChernozhukovLeeRosen2013 localizes binding inequalities for intersection bounds and calibrates Gaussian extrema, but does not address exact zero-cell multinomial support adaptation.
HuangEtAl2019 constructs confidence intervals for a two-arm ordinal fraction-benefiting bound, while the related plug-in literature leaves difficult boundary behavior unresolved.
literature_map.settled: Directional limit maps, perturbed-LP coverage, and active-contact localization are settled in their respective regularity regimes.
literature_map.unoccupied_target: No located procedure combines finite-sample multinomial honesty for changing support and tied faces across six coordinates with scalar semiparametric efficiency on separated positive-support faces.
